cards.headline: The scientific method in one breath
lines: Ask a question, propose a testable explanation, and predict what should happen.
Run a test that could prove you wrong.
Keep the idea only if it survives — and share it so others can try to break it.
cards.source: Popper, 'The Logic of Scientific Discovery' (1959); standard science curricula.

cards.headline: Everything is made of atoms
lines: An atom has a tiny, dense nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it.
The number of protons sets the element: 1 is hydrogen, 6 is carbon, 8 is oxygen.
Atoms are mostly empty space.

cards.headline: DNA is a four-letter code
lines: DNA stores genetic instructions using four bases: A, T, C and G.
A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so each strand can rebuild the other.
Watson and Crick described the double helix in 1953, using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data.
cards.source: Watson & Crick (1953), Nature; Alberts et al., 'Molecular Biology of the Cell'.

cards.headline: Energy changes form but isn't lost
lines: Conservation of energy: energy can change form, but the total stays the same.
A falling ball turns height (potential energy) into speed (kinetic energy).
Some always ends up as heat — which is why no machine is 100% efficient.

cards.headline: Light is fast, but not instant
lines: Light travels about 300,000 km every second in a vacuum.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.
So you always see the Sun as it was a few minutes ago.
cards.source: NIST/CODATA value of c (299,792,458 m/s); NASA Sun fact sheet.

cards.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
cards.why: Two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

cards.question: In photosynthesis, plants use light to turn carbon dioxide and water into…
cards.why: Plants build glucose and release oxygen as a by-product.

cards.question: A feather and a hammer are dropped together in a vacuum. How do they fall?
options: They fall at the same rate
cards.why: Without air resistance, gravity accelerates everything equally. Apollo 15's David Scott showed it on the Moon in 1971.
cards.source: NASA Apollo 15 mission record; Halliday, Resnick & Walker.

cards.question: At sea level, pure water boils at…
cards.why: 100 °C (212 °F). Higher up, lower air pressure means water boils at a lower temperature.

cards.question: In an animal cell, where is most of the DNA kept?
cards.why: DNA is packaged in the nucleus. Mitochondria carry a small amount of their own.
cards.source: Alberts et al., 'Molecular Biology of the Cell'.

cards.headline: By count, you're mostly hydrogen atoms
cards.text: About 60% of the atoms in a human body are hydrogen — largely because so much of us is water.
cards.source: Emsley, 'Nature's Building Blocks'; standard human body composition tables.

cards.headline: Sealed honey keeps for years
cards.text: Honey's low water content and acidity stop most microbes from growing, so it barely spoils when kept sealed.
cards.source: Food chemistry references; National Honey Board.

cards.headline: Diamond and pencil 'lead' are both pure carbon
cards.text: In diamond, carbon atoms lock into a rigid 3D lattice. In graphite they form flat sheets that slide — so one scratches glass and the other smudges paper.
cards.source: Atkins & Jones, 'Chemical Principles', allotropes of carbon.

cards.headline: Sound travels about 343 m every second
cards.text: That's in air at 20 °C. Count the seconds between lightning and thunder, divide by 3, and you have the distance in kilometres.
cards.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, 'Fundamentals of Physics', sound waves.

cards.headline: Natural selection in four steps

steps.headline: 1 · Variation
lines: Individuals differ — in size, colour, speed and more.
Some of those differences are inherited.

steps.headline: 2 · Too many offspring
lines: Most species produce more young than can survive.
So individuals compete for food, space and mates.

steps.headline: 3 · Selection
lines: Traits that help an individual survive and reproduce get passed on more often.
Darwin and Wallace proposed this together in 1858.

steps.headline: 4 · Change over time
lines: Over many generations, helpful traits become more common.
Example: bacteria evolving resistance to antibiotics.

cards.source: Darwin, 'On the Origin of Species' (1859); Futuyma, 'Evolution'.

cards.headline: Science: the takeaways
points: Science tests ideas that could be proven wrong.
Atoms: a nucleus with electrons around it.
DNA pairs A with T, C with G.
Energy changes form but isn't lost.
The sunlight you see is about 8 minutes old.
